claims.text: AlNbTiZr medium-entropy-alloy coatings can be deposited on zirconium-alloy cladding by RF magnetron co-sputtering.
An Al content of about 10 at.% is optimal among the tested AlNbTiZr coating compositions.
A coating containing 10.2 at.% Al had the best corrosion resistance among AlNbTiZr coatings with different Al contents.
About 10 at.% Al will significantly improve high-temperature steam oxidation resistance relative to coatings with lower or higher Al contents.
The intervention should work during steam exposure at approximately 800 °C for tens of hours.
Approximately 800 °C steam exposure is representative of loss-of-coolant-accident conditions relevant to the proposed coating.
The optimized coating forms a dense oxide layer consisting mainly of Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2.
The protective composite oxide layer is finely grained.
Optimizing the Al content promotes selective oxidation.
The resulting oxide scale is stable and adherent.
The denser oxide layer impedes oxygen transport and reduces further oxidation.
The 10.2 at.% Al coating has a smaller oxygen penetration depth than the other tested Al-content variants.
Under high-temperature steam, the approximately 10 at.% Al coating will have lower weight gain and shallower oxygen penetration than uncoated zirconium alloy.
Under high-temperature steam, the approximately 10 at.% Al coating will have lower weight gain and shallower oxygen penetration than both lower- and higher-Al AlNbTiZr coatings.
The intervention enhances oxidation protection without adversely affecting other service properties of the cladding.
The intervention remains effective up to approximately 800–900 °C in steam.
At higher temperatures or under prolonged irradiation, additional degradation mechanisms may affect coating performance.
The optimum Al content may shift with deposition parameters and long-term in-reactor conditions.
The effects of irradiation and thermal gradients on oxide-scale stability are not fully quantified.
